Jenoptik.why: supplies optics for lithography and semiconductor-inspection systems; its Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing unit, by far its largest, is driven by the semi equipment ramp
Jenoptik.evidence: Jenoptik Q2 FY2026 call (08-12-2026): CFO - Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing revenue up around 10%, driven by lithography and semi-inspection; Jena clean-room capacity caters to inspection and lithography customers

players.product: precision optical modules and classical optics for lithography and semiconductor-inspection equipment (Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: revenue up 1% year-on-year (close to 3% excluding currency); EBITDA around EUR 99 million, up a little more than 25%, margin up almost 400 basis points; EBIT up 56%, margin 12.3%; EPS EUR 0.69 (prior year EUR 0.42). Group order intake up more than 50% year-on-year, exceeding expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +1%; EBITDA around EUR 99 million; EBIT margin 12.3%; EPS EUR 0.69

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised to the upper half of the initial ranges: FY2026 revenue growth of 5% to 9% and EBITDA margin of 20% to 21% (original 19%-21%), mainly because Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing is developing better than expected; capex still expected slightly below last year. CFO: some orders came surprisingly early, so the very strong order intake may not continue in the next two quarters.

H1 2026 book-to-bill rose to 1.4 and the order backlog grew to around EUR 825 million. CFO: semi order intake was driven by lithography and continued strong semi-inspection activity; Q2 was a little below Q1, which had a large annual order; some customers in a semi ramp-up may order to secure capacity, but this is not a pull-forward from H2.

Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing (by far the largest unit): H1 revenue up around 10%, driven by lithography and semi-inspection, with an EBITDA margin of close to 32%. CFO: the semi ramp-up is 'in full swing'; after the 2025 supply-chain adjustments the lithography business is expected to grow; if semi is firing on all cylinders the margin can land 'a tad above' the roughly 30% range, with lagging factor costs (German collective agreement, added FTEs).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue up around 10%; EBITDA margin close to 32%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (CFO): the near-term focus is capacity expansion in the OEM businesses and maximizing output; machines and people are being added; the Dresden fab (online since early 2025, ramped slower than planned) is being ramped further; in Jena an additional classical-optics facility came online at the beginning of 2026 and further high-precision clean-room capacity serving inspection and lithography customers is underway but will not affect the next couple of quarters. The supply chain is ramping in lockstep and is not tangibly constrained so far.

CFO: Jenoptik does not sell to Chinese suppliers in its semi business, a strategic decision made a couple of years ago that remains intact. Optical data communications (microlens arrays) shows growing demand and revenue on a significantly smaller base, serving multiple customers.

Other units, H1 2026: Biophotonics order intake +45% (defense demand and a multi-year MedTech order in the low double-digit million range), revenue down almost 5%, margin almost 22%; Smart Mobility Solutions revenue up almost 11%; Metrology & Production Solutions slightly loss-making on weak European automotive, with H2 expected better than H1. A strategy review is under way, with findings expected towards the end of 2026 at the earliest.
quarterly_data.figure: Biophotonics order intake +45%; SMS revenue up almost 11%
